title: wt remove <work> --dry-run --json
description: What `wt remove <work>` would do, and the token that holds a later removal to it. Printed by `wt remove <work> --dry-run --json`, and by `wt remove <work> --json` without --yes, as the only thing on stdout; nothing is changed. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows: minor for an added field or enumeration value, patch for wording.

repo.description: The main checkout; null outside a repository.

trunkSource.description: Since 1.3.0. How trunk was found, as in the other plans (see docs/json.md, trunkSource); null with trunk.

token.description: Names this plan; pass it to wt remove --yes --json --expect. Null when the removal would refuse, or on error.

error.description: Why the removal would refuse, or why no plan could be made.

adminDir.description: The worktree's own git dir, .git/worktrees/<id>; null when it cannot be read.

head.description: The commit checked out; null before the first commit.

detached.description: No branch is checked out: no branch is touched.

branch.description: The branch checked out; null when detached.

bases.description: What merged is measured against, first first: origin/<trunk> as last fetched, then <trunk>. Remove never fetches.

dirty.description: Anything uncommitted, submodules included, whatever git's config says.

statusError.description: Why the status could not be read; the removal refuses.

hiddenFiles.description: Unedited files git status is told not to look at (assume-unchanged, skip-worktree).

movedSubmodules.description: Submodules checked out at another commit than the recorded one.

nestedWorktrees.description: Other worktrees whose checkouts are inside this one.

operation.description: A git operation stopped halfway there; sequencer is a cherry-pick or revert sequence whose HEAD marker is gone.

sessions.description: {id, name, kind, pid, state} for each agent session in the checkout, other than the one running wt: kind claude or codex (since 1.4.0), state idle or busy.

sessionsError.description: Why the sessions could not be listed; the removal refuses without --force.

lock.description: Git's lock on the worktree: reason, holder (who wt worked out is behind it), pid, and held (still running; a stale one is released).

unreachable.description: Each tip nothing surviving the removal holds, with kind, oid, count, path and restoreCommand. A branch is the branch the removal deletes: listed, not refused, with the git branch argv that brings its commits back. head and submodule (with path) refuse.

reachError.description: Why that could not be worked out; the removal refuses.

keepSuperset.description: Since 1.1.0. --keep-superset was given: the worktree's Superset workspace is left, and Superset is not asked anything. The token covers it.

processes.description: Since 1.5.0. The processes working in the checkout, or in a directory inside it, that wt does not spare: a dev server, a watcher, a language server. Spared and never listed: another user's processes, any with a controlling terminal, wt itself with its children and ancestors, and agent processes, Claude's and Codex's, the caller's own included. Empty when there are none, or when they could not be found (processesError says why). Removal ends them only with --reap; the token covers them then. reap is true with --reap, which ends it before the checkout goes, and false without, when it is left running.

processesError.description: Since 1.5.0. Why the processes could not be found: the process table could not be read, or the agent sessions could not be listed, so none is known to be safe to end. With --reap this refuses the removal (problem processesUnknown), whatever --force says; without it the removal goes ahead and leaves them. With --reap that refuses (processesUnknown).

force.description: Bare --force was given: the problems with force true do not refuse. False for --force=<list>, whose categories forceWith names.

forceWith.description: Since 1.2.0. The --force categories given, all five for bare --force; empty without it. The token covers them.

problems.description: Every problem with the removal; those that refuse it are all of them, less the ones whose forceWith is in the top-level forceWith.

code.description: dirty: anything uncommitted, submodules included, or a submodule not at its recorded commit. statusUnknown: git status, the git dir or HEAD could not be read. session: an agent session is in it, idle or busy. sessionsUnknown: the sessions could not be listed. lockHeld: git's worktree lock, and its holder is still running. operation: a rebase, merge, cherry-pick, revert or bisect in progress. hiddenChanges: files git status is told not to look at. headUnreachable: HEAD holds commits no surviving ref or worktree would. reachUnknown: what would be lost could not be worked out. submoduleUnreachable: a submodule commit only this worktree's copy holds. nestedWorktree: another worktree is inside it. staleForcedPush: a remote.<name>.push refspec with + would force a plain git push from the kept copy over a remote branch that moved on; nothing is changed (since 1.6.0). quarantineUnusable: the --move-to folder exists, is on another volume, or is inside the repository. processesUnknown: with --reap, the processes in it could not be found or told apart from agent sessions; no --force goes past it. planChanged (result only): --expect named another plan. The codes shared with sweep-plan's kept mean the same there.

force.description: --force goes past it: somebody's claim on the checkout, not work that would be lost.

forceWith.description: Since 1.2.0. The --force category that goes past it; null when force is false. A session problem is either idle-sessions or busy-sessions: idle and busy sessions are two problems. Null when force is false (since 1.2.0).

forceCategory.description: What --force=<list> names; bare --force is all of them. idle-sessions: an idle agent session in it. busy-sessions: a busy one, and idle ones too. sessions-unknown: the sessions could not be listed. hidden-files: files git status is told not to look at, unedited. lock: git's lock, its holder still running.

tip.description: Null when the branch is already gone.

merge.description: merged: base contains the tip. applied: every commit is on base under another id, byte for byte. unmerged: base lacks commits of it. unknown: no trunk to compare with, or the branch is gone.

base.description: The base the standing is about.

ahead.description: Commits base lacks; meaningful for unmerged and applied.

pullRequest.description: A pull request GitHub merged into trunk at exactly tip, as wt list or wt sweep recorded it; it makes an unmerged branch deletable.

outcome.description: delete: merged, applied or pullRequest; deleted after the checkout, only at tip. keep: an unmerged branch wt made; renamed to keepAs. none: left as it is; reason says why. The same names recovery.json's branch.plan uses.

refspec.description: For via refspec: the setting, remote.<name>.push=<refspec>. Null otherwise.

staleRoutes.description: Since 1.6.0. For outcome keep: every remote branch the kept copy could push to that holds commits the branch lacks, as last fetched, each with how it would get there and what the removal does about it. via: recorded (where wt records or infers the branch pushes; it goes with the rename), upstream (the upstream, where push.default sends a plain push to it), sameName (the kept name on the remote a plain push goes to), refspec (a remote.<name>.push refspec, as remote.<name>.push=<refspec>, which wt does not change: it is the remote's, shared by every checkout). dropped: the removal takes that route away by removing the branch's own setting; false: it stays, and git refuses a plain push unless forced. forces: a refspec with +, which a plain push follows over a branch that moved on; that refuses the removal (problem staleForcedPush) and nothing is changed. The token covers every route and the commit compared. Empty when none, or the branch is not kept.

id.description: Claude's session id. For a Codex session, codex-<pid> for a codex process working in the checkout, the thread id for a thread an app-server runs.

holder.description: Whoever wt worked out is behind it.

held.description: Its holder is still there. A held lock refuses without --force; a stale one is released.

kind.description: branch: the branch the removal deletes; listed, not refused. head: the checkout's HEAD; refuses. submodule: a submodule's commits; refuses.

path.description: For submodule: the submodule, relative to the checkout.

restoreCommand.description: For branch: the git branch argv that brings the commits back once the branch is gone, to run in the repository (git -C <repo> branch <name> <oid>).

command.description: Its command line as ps shows it, arguments joined with spaces.

reap.description: --reap was given: the removal ends it, SIGTERM and then SIGKILL after 5 seconds, before the checkout goes. False: it is left running.
